original_test_intent: Verify BMC I2C-6 reaches the I2C switch on each carrier board and that each switch exposes the expected identity/control state and downstream endpoints without changing routing.
original_method: Map BMC I2C-6 to bus5 and identify both carrier-board switch instances, including mux/segment selection if they share0x73; capture driver ownership and routing state; read each switch control byte through the supported path; validate expected value/mask and PID-defined downstream address-specific replies per board; preserve routing and confirm sibling board/BMC health.
manual_activity: BMC/carrier owner supplies the per-board switch topology/selection, expected control states and downstream oracle, plus ownership and recovery; physical probing is not inferred.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping of BMC I2C-6 to Linux bus5 and both carrier-board switch instances
Method to distinguish/select board A and board B if both use0x73
Switch part/revision, control-register semantics and expected read byte/mask for each board
PID-defined non-mutating downstream endpoint/address/reply matrix per carrier board
Kernel/daemon driver binding and whether force access is permitted
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, route-state preservation/restoration and independent BMC recovery
safety_requirements: Do not assume one0x73 ACK represents both boards
Do not use quick-write discovery broadly; query only approved instances/endpoints
Avoid `-f` while a switch driver/daemon owns the device unless explicitly approved
Read but do not change channel/routing control; record and verify original state
Abort on instance ambiguity, state change, NACK, timeout, stuck bus, downstream loss or BMC degradation
agent_execution_scope: Collect carrier identities, switch topology, owner and original control/downstream state
After approval, read each identified switch and approved downstream endpoints separately
Do not probe/solder, scan blindly, select boards by guess, write switch channels, force a bound device, auto-retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve two-board instance-selection and BMC I2C-6/bus5 map
Approve control-byte and downstream response oracle per board
Approve driver-safe access, timeouts and recovery/restoration
Review separate board-A/board-B evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; source supplies a functional switch read.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not use broad `i2cdetect -q`. Retain `i2cget -f -y 5 0x73` only after resolving which board instance it selects and owner approval for `-f`; repeat through the authoritative selection path for the other board and add only PID-defined downstream reads without changing channels.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus5, address0x73, BMC I2C-6, both carrier-board switches, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Collect a separate read-only switch/control/downstream evidence set for each carrier board while preserving routing.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes two-instance coverage measurable, adds downstream proof and ownership controls, and removes invented physical probing and unsafe generic scanning.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One switch control byte confirms only the currently addressed instance and current channel mask; it does not prove the second carrier switch or either board's downstream connectivity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Forced access can race platform management and switch routing; identical addresses require an upstream selector whose state must be known and preserved.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires controller/bus, each target instance/address, expected replies and OOB recovery. Multi-instance aliasing must be explicitly resolved rather than inferred from one address.
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-6/bus5 and board-A/board-B switch selection paths
Both carrier-board and switch part/revision identities plus owner/driver state
Original and expected switch control-byte matrix for each selected instance
Per-board downstream endpoint expected-versus-observed read matrix with timestamps/status
Evidence selection/routing did not change and sibling board remained reachable
Pre/post BMC/bus health plus engineer verdict for each board and overall

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source asks for two switches but supplies one ambiguous0x73 read and no expected value or downstream criteria. It also omits instance selection/ownership and earlier reviews invent physical probing.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The two-board functional intent is clear; owner-supplied topology, expected states and safe access make it executable, so this is RPUC.

Approve/replace broad scan and `-f`, define ownership, timeouts, no-route-change verification/restoration and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Changes the physical-only verdict into a two-instance functional test and makes explicit that one shared address/read cannot satisfy both carrier-board paths.
independent_technical_reasoning: The plural scope is the distinguishing requirement. If both boards expose0x73 behind a selector, an unqualified read reaches only whichever segment is active; if there is a single upstream0x73, it still cannot prove downstream switches on both boards. Therefore each board needs authoritative selection, its own control-state evidence and downstream responses while preserving routing. This is remotely testable once topology and ownership are known, with no mandatory probe step.
